10.2139/ssrn.5166467.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive techno-economic analysis of renewable energy-powered ammonia production in Denmark. The study employs numerical simulation to optimize the design parameters of an integrated system consisting of wind turbines, photovoltaic arrays, electrolyzers, batteries, and hydrogen storage. The objective is to minimize the Levelized Cost of Ammonia (LCOA) while maintaining system reliability. Utilizing meteorological data for renewable resource assessment, the model evaluates multiple system configurations through parametric optimization. Results demonstrate that a well-balanced system with 212,923 kW of wind capacity, 85,169 kW of solar capacity, 145,370 kW of electrolyzer capacity, 19,096 kWh of battery storage, and 237,339 kg of hydrogen storage capacity can achieve an LCOA of 103.79 USD/ton. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to decarbonize the ammonia industry, providing valuable insights for policy makers and industrial stakeholders interested in renewable-based ammonia production.

10.2139/ssrn.5277239.abstract: The separation of ammonia from aqueous solutions is a critical process in environmental engineering and industrial applications. In this study, we investigate the use of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) membranes for ammonia separation in a liquid membrane system. The proposed system consists of three vital layers. The central layer acting as a PDMS membrane and the other two outer layers on each side containing flowing ammonia in liquid form. Using COMSOL Multiphysics modelling, the diffusion of ammonia through the PDMS membrane under various operating conditions were studied. The study focused to analyse the effect of the ammonia concentration in the membrane system by varying the concentration from 100 mg/L to 200 mg/L in the intervals of 25 mg/L. On top that, the impacts of varying different partition coefficient were also observed. The partition coefficient varied was 0.05, 0.1 and 0.5. The parameters such as pressure field and velocity were also examined to understand the dynamics of the ammonia diffusion process. Obtained results provides insights into the concentration profiles, velocity fields, and pressure distributions across the membrane system. Findings concluded that the PDMS membranes offer promising performance for ammonia separation, with potential for optimization through partition coefficient and the concentration of the ammonia used in the membrane system. From the series of findings, it is clear that the efficiency of the ammonia diffusion process depends solely on the ideal choice of membrane and its operating conditions. Increasing the ammonia inflow concentration from 100 mg/L to 200 mg/L resulted in higher surface concentrations on the PDMS membrane. This finding highlights the impact of inflow concentration on the membrane's absorption capacity and separation performance.

10.59717/j.xinn-energy.2025.100122.abstract: Ammonia, as a key feedstock for nitrogen fertilizers, also plays a crucial role as an energy and hydrogen carrier in the storage and conversion of renewable energy. The synthesis and decomposition of ammonia are central to realizing its full potential in these applications. Recent studies have highlighted the versatile chemical interconversions of alkali/alkaline metal hydrides, amides, and imides exhibit with N2, H2, or NH3. Building on these findings, a series of highly efficient catalysts and novel processes for ammonia synthesis and ammonia decomposition have been developed. This review comprehensively summarizes recent progress in utilizing these compounds as functional materials for catalytic and chemical looping processes in ammonia synthesis and decomposition. Special attention is given to the unique roles of hydrides, amides, and imides in activating and transforming N2 and NH3, their distinct reaction mechanisms, and discuss the current challenges and future prospects of these materials in ammonia synthesis and decomposition process.

10.7868/s3034553725020205.abstract: The electrochemical reaction reduction of nitrites (NO2−RR) in a neutral aqueous electrolyte is studied, which has important applications both for future ammonia synthesis processes and for effective wastewater and agricultural wastewater treatment. The catalytic activity is compared (the results of the Faradaic efficiency and the yield rate of ammonia are obtained) for noble (platinum) and non-noble (cobalt) metals. Metallic polycrystalline platinum and cobalt serve as electrocatalyst. The surface of the catalysts is analyzed using SEM and light microscopy. The method of linear voltammetry is used to preliminarily identify the potential of ammonia synthesis and estimate the synthesis current density. The values of Faradaic efficiency (FE) and the yield rate of ammonia release are obtained for the five selected values of current densities (J). It is found that the cobalt cathode is more efficient (FE ≈ 99%, yield rate (NH3) = 2.4 mmol h–1 cm–2), which exceeds the values for the platinum cathode ((FE = 88.1%, yield rate (NH3) = 0.4 mmol h–1 cm–2). The electrochemically active surface (ECSA) of the electrocatalysts is determined. The explanation of such activity of catalysts is given according to the results of the work that demonstrate that a non-noble metal cathode can be more effective for NO2−RR.

10.7868/s3034560x25090115.abstract: Ti–Sc–O thin films were synthesized at 300°C by atomic layer deposition (ALD) via alternating between the reaction cycles with metal precursors and HO as co-reactant. By varying the cycle ratio, the materials of [Sc]/([Ti] + [Sc]) = 13, 25, 44, 64, 82% were obtained. The films were examined via spectral and single wave null ellipsometry, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. The formation of the material was demonstrated to be substrate-inhibited and to occur within the “temperature window” of ALD. As a result of Ti2p and Sc2p XPS spectra analysis, the oxidation states of the metals are Ti and Sc. At low Sc concentrations (up to [Sc]/([Ti] + [Sc]) = 25%) the film crystallization into anatase phase observed for individual TiO film is suppressed. In the range of [Sc]/([Ti] + [Sc]) = 44–100% the materials of various cubic crystal structure types are formed: with the increase of scandium concentration the structure changes from disordered fluorite ScTiO to cubic ScO-based solid solution. The refractive indices (), extinction coefficients () and optical bandgap values are well described by the Tauc-Lorentz model. They vary between the corresponding parameters of the individual oxides depending on the composition, which is relevant for current problems of optics, photonics, solar energy and photocatalysis.
